A rare recessive ataxic disorder is identified in several unrelated families. Patient-derived Purkinje neurons (from iPSC differentiation) show the following consistent abnormalities.

Normal passive membrane properties and resting potential, but a significantly increased input resistance during sustained depolarization, without changes in \({Na^+}\) or \({K^+}\) conductances.

Climbing-fiber–evoked \({Ca}^{2+}\) spikes are normal in amplitude but decay nearly twice as slowly, accompanied by prolonged after hyperpolarization.

Parallel-fiber long-term depression (LTD) and rebound potentiation are both intact, yet climbing-fiber–evoked complex spikes show progressive broadening during trains at \(1\) Hz.

Normal expression of \({Cav2.1}\), \({IP3R1}\), \({SERCA2}\), and \({calbindin-D28k}\); however, high-resolution immuno-EM shows selective mislocalization of \({Ca}^{2+}\)-ATPase pumps and \({Na^+}\)/\({Ca}^{2+}\) exchangers away from distal dendritic spines and toward the soma.

Reveals marked downregulation of a single ER–plasma membrane tethering protein, which normally binds \({VAPB}\) and \({ORAI1}\), coupling store-operated \({Ca}^{2+}\) entry to local microdomain refilling in Purkinje dendrites.

Which single molecular target best explains this pattern of mislocalized \({Ca}^{2+}\) signaling and abnormal Purkinje dendritic excitability?

A patient presents with exercise intolerance and progressive optic neuropathy. 

Muscle biopsy shows partial deficiency of mitochondrial complex I. 

Mitochondrial RNA sequencing reveals global shortening of the \(5'\) ends of several mRNAs and rRNAs without changes in steady-state transcript abundance. 

In vitro assays demonstrate impaired ribosome assembly despite normal RNA folding predictions. 

Dysfunction of which mitochondrial RNA helicase most parsimoniously explains these observations?

Progressive \(\alpha\)-synuclein fibrillization, combined with chronic mitochondrial bioenergetic deficits in substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons, initiates a cascade of reactive oxygen species accumulation, neuroinflammation, and proteostasis impairment. Nuclear epigenetic machinery, including \(DNA\) methyltransferases, \(TET\) enzymes, and histone-modifying complexes, together responds to metabolic, redox, and one-carbon metabolite fluctuations. Cummulatively, they modulates the chromatin accessibility at neuroprotective, stress-response, and plasticity-associated loci. Concurrently, mitochondrial \(DNA\) methylation, nucleoid architecture, and mitochondrial epigenetic modifiers fine-tune transcription of electron transport chain components and antioxidant genes. Persistent disturbances in \(SAM/SAH\) balance, environmental toxins, and chronic stress induce locus-specific hypermethylation at \(PARKIN\), \(PINK1\), and \(TFAM\) promoters. While activity-dependent demethylation transiently activates \(BDNF\) and other plasticity genes, the sustained, bidirectional coordination between nuclear chromatin remodeling and mitochondrial epigenetic modifications consolidates long-term transcriptional repression. Unlike transient signaling events, this process establishes stable vulnerability and impaired cellular resilience across compartments.

Which molecular mechanism orchestrates the coordination of nuclear chromatin remodeling with mitochondrial epigenetic modifications to establish enduring transcriptional repression?

A hepatocyte line overexpressing the ER-resident chaperone protein X exhibits mild UPR activation, altered ER sheet-to-tubule ratio, and selective retention of GPI-anchored proteins. Concurrently, a point mutation in the \(5\) prime splice site of exon \(6\) of Gene M leads to exon skipping and unexpected intron retention in several transcripts encoding RNA-binding proteins. Interestingly, RNA-seq reveals that some intron-retaining mRNAs are exported and translated, producing truncated proteins that interact with transcription factors regulating ER stress genes. ChIP-seq of these transcription factors shows co-occupancy at super-enhancers along with non-coding RNAs that scaffold Polycomb complexes, while ATAC-seq indicates decreased chromatin accessibility at these loci. Paradoxically, global secretion and cell viability remain largely unaffected, yet lipidomics shows accumulation of lyso-phosphatidylcholine species and a shift in ER membrane curvature. Based on the observations, propose a mechanistic explanation linking ER lipid remodeling, selective protein retention, aberrant splicing, and transcriptional rewiring, considering potential feedback loops, RNA-mediated scaffolding, and organelle cross-talk.

In recent experiments investigating secondary resistance mechanisms to \(5'\)-fluoroorotic acid (\(\text{5'-FOA}\)) in \(\textit{Saccharomyces cerevisiae}\), researchers observed a rare class of mutants that survived selection despite maintaining an intact \(\textit{URA3}\) locus. Transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling suggested a compensatory reconfiguration of pyrimidine metabolism involving the \(\text{UMP}\) salvage shunt and altered regulation of nucleotide pool homeostasis. Surprisingly, these resistant isolates showed significant downregulation of a gene encoding a cytosolic phosphatase that normally hydrolyzes excess uridine monophosphate (\(\text{UMP}\)) and orotidine monophosphate (\(\text{OMP}\)), balancing nucleotide turnover under nutrient stress. Structural modeling of the mutant protein revealed that resistance-associated substitutions disrupt the metal-binding loop required for phosphate cleavage, effectively trapping \(\text{UMP}\) analogs in a non-toxic monophosphorylated state and preventing their conversion into lethal \(5\)-fluorouridine nucleotides. Evolutionary conservation of this locus across \(Ascomycota\) species hinted at a broader metabolic buffering role under nucleotide analog stress, distinct from canonical \(\textit{URA3}\) inactivation. Further, targeted deletion of this gene phenocopied \(\text{FOA}\) resistance, while its overexpression restored drug sensitivity, confirming its pivotal regulatory function in fluoropyrimidine detoxification. Which gene, encoding a pyrimidine monophosphatase that indirectly modulates \(\text{5'-FOA}\) sensitivity in yeast through control of nucleotide pool turnover, confers resistance when inactivated?
